01.event: Rabbi Abbahu moved an oil lamp on Shabbat in Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi's town but refrained from doing so in Rabbi Yohanan's town.
01.turn: His inconsistent behavior is explained as deference to Rabbi Yohanan in his own locale, and his servant, who might be confused, had to be told why.
01.outcome: He informed his servant of the reason for the change in behavior.
01.summary: Rabbi Abbahu, who held it permitted to move a burnt-out oil lamp on Shabbat, did so when visiting Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi's town. When he visited Rabbi Yohanan's town, where it was forbidden, he refrained out of respect for Rabbi Yohanan. To keep his servant from drawing the wrong conclusion, he explained to him why he acted differently there.
01.missing: This is a recurring habit rather than a single event; the servant explanation is the Gemara's resolution, not a narrated scene.

02.event: Rav arrived at the house of the son of a vinegar strainer and examined the family.
02.turn: The examination was of whether they fell silent in quarrels, not of their genealogy.
02.summary: Rav once came to the household of a vinegar strainer's son and had its members examined. According to the Gemara, he told the examiners to check whether the family members fell silent when they quarreled, a sign of good lineage.
02.missing: The result of the examination and any consequence for the family are not given.

04.event: In an actual case, Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi gave an orphan girl one-twelfth of her late father's property as her dowry.
04.outcome: She received one-twelfth rather than the standard one-tenth.
04.summary: Rav Adda bar Ahava reported that in one case Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi awarded an orphaned daughter one-twelfth of her father's estate for her dowry. The Gemara explains that the father's wishes had been assessed in that case.
04.missing: The details of the case and the parties are not given; it is reported only as a ruling.

05.actor: An Arab and his camel, as witnessed by Rabba bar bar Hanna
05.event: Rabba bar bar Hanna saw an Arab take his sword and cut open his camel.
05.turn: The camel died so fast that it did not even finish braying.
05.outcome: The camel died instantly; Abaye later explained it was emaciated.
05.summary: Rabba bar bar Hanna recounted that he once saw an Arab slash open his camel with a sword. The camel died so quickly that it had not stopped braying. Abaye explained that the camel must have been weak and emaciated.

06.actor: The widow of Rav Yosef son of Rav Menashya of D'vil
06.event: The widow came before Rav Yosef and asked him to allot her sustenance, wine, and then silk garments.
06.turn: When he asked why she needed silk, she retorted that it was for him and his colleagues.
06.outcome: Her answer stands as the last word: she should not be shamed before the scholars.
06.summary: A widow came before Rav Yosef and asked him to allocate support for her from her late husband's estate. He granted her food and wine. When she also demanded silk garments and he asked why, she answered that it was for him, his friends and his friends' friends, meaning she should not appear shabby before the sages.
06.missing: Whether he granted the silk is not stated.

07.event: The Sages asked Rabbi Abbahu where Rabbi Elai was hiding.
07.turn: Rabbi Abbahu answered with a cryptic, punning riddle.
07.outcome: His answer implied Rabbi Elai was asleep after a night kept awake by a lively young woman.
07.summary: The Sages, unable to find Rabbi Elai, asked Rabbi Abbahu where he was. Rabbi Abbahu replied with a riddle full of wordplay: Rabbi Elai had rejoiced with a lively young woman of priestly descent who kept him awake. The point is that Rabbi Elai was sleeping.
07.missing: It is an exchange with a witty answer; there is no further event or resolution.

08.actor: Rav Pappa and Rav Huna son of Rav Yehoshua
08.event: Rav Pappa and Rav Huna were about to permit a nursing mother to remarry immediately, following a baraita.
08.turn: An old woman told them Rav Nahman had forbidden it in her own case, and Rav Pappi reminded them of a baraita and a ruling that the halakha follows Rabbi Meir's decrees.
08.outcome: They admitted they had forgotten the principle.
08.summary: Rav Pappa and Rav Huna son of Rav Yehoshua were about to rule, based on a baraita, that a woman who had handed her baby to a wet nurse could remarry right away. An old woman stopped them, saying that Rav Nahman had forbidden exactly this in her case. Rav Pappi then pointed out a baraita requiring all women to wait three months, and Shmuel's rule that the halakha follows Rabbi Meir's decrees. The two sages admitted they had not had this in mind.

09.event: A case came before Rabbi Yitzhak in Antioch.
09.outcome: He ruled that collection by oath in the husband's absence applies only to a marriage contract, not to a creditor.
09.summary: Rav Aha Sar HaBira reported that a case came before Rabbi Yitzhak in Antioch. Rabbi Yitzhak ruled that a woman may collect her marriage contract with an oath in her husband's absence, but a creditor may not collect a debt that way.
09.missing: The facts of the case itself are not given; only the ruling is reported.

10.actor: Rabbi Elai, Rabbi Ya'akov bar Zavdi and Rabbi Shimon bar Abba
10.event: Rabbi Shimon bar Abba passed by two sages who were studying, and they stood up for him.
10.turn: He told them they should not have stood: they were ordained and he was not, and the Torah does not rise before its students.
10.outcome: He rebuked their gesture of respect as unnecessary.
10.summary: Rabbi Elai and Rabbi Ya'akov bar Zavdi were sitting and studying when Rabbi Shimon bar Abba walked by, and they rose for him. He told them there was no need: they were ordained scholars while he was only an associate, and in any case people engaged in Torah study need not stand before those who study it.

11.actor: A man from Eretz Yisrael and Rabbi Hanina
11.event: A man whose brother had died leaving a widow in Bei Hoza'a in Babylonia asked Rabbi Hanina whether he could go down to perform levirate marriage.
11.turn: Rabbi Hanina condemned the dead brother for leaving the land and marrying abroad, blessing God for killing him.
11.outcome: He told the man not to follow his brother out of Eretz Yisrael.
11.summary: A man in Eretz Yisrael learned that his childless brother had died, leaving a widow in distant Bei Hoza'a whom he was obligated to marry or release. He asked Rabbi Hanina whether he could travel to Babylonia to marry her. Rabbi Hanina replied harshly that the brother had married a foreign woman and died, blessed be God who killed him, and asked whether the man now wanted to go down after him.

12.actor: A woman litigant, Rav Beivai bar Abaye and Rav Pappi
12.event: A woman obliged to take an oath in Rav Beivai bar Abaye's court asked for a document of rights in advance before agreeing to swear in town.
12.turn: Rav Beivai ordered the document written for her before the oath.
12.outcome: Rav Pappi mocked the ruling, saying Rav Beivai spoke unfortunate words because he came from an unfortunate family.
12.summary: A woman was required to take an oath in Rav Beivai bar Abaye's court, and her opponent asked that she swear publicly in town, hoping shame would make her confess. She agreed only if the court first wrote her a document of rights that would be handed over once she swore. Rav Beivai told the scribes to write it. Rav Pappi sharply criticized the decision, jibing that Rav Beivai's descent from an ill-fated family led him to say ill-fated things.

13.event: Villagers asked Rabbi Yirmeya whether one may make an eiruv with moist beans, and he did not know.
13.turn: Back at the study hall he was told Rabbi Yannai's ruling.
13.outcome: He learned that moist beans are permitted, in the amount of a handful.
13.summary: Rabbi Yirmeya once visited some villages, where the people asked him whether an eiruv could be made with moist beans. He did not know the answer. When he returned to the study hall, his colleagues told him that Rabbi Yannai permitted it, and Rav Yehiel specified a handful as the amount.

14.actor: The judges of Neharde'a, Rav Hana bar Bizna and Rav Nahman
14.event: Judges in Neharde'a and Rav Hana bar Bizna in Pumbedita ruled that daughters be supported from movable property.
14.turn: Rav Nahman ordered them to reverse their rulings or he would seize their houses.
14.summary: In Neharde'a the local judges, and in Pumbedita Rav Hana bar Bizna, ruled that orphan daughters must be supported from their father's movable property, and collected accordingly. Rav Nahman told them to undo their decisions, threatening to take their own houses to compensate the heirs otherwise.
14.missing: Whether the judges complied is not stated.

15.event: Judges ruled a case according to Rabbi Tarfon, and Reish Lakish overturned their ruling.
15.turn: Rabbi Yohanan criticized Reish Lakish for reversing it.
15.outcome: Rabbi Yohanan told him he had treated the matter as if it were Torah law.
15.summary: Some judges decided an inheritance case following Rabbi Tarfon's view, and Reish Lakish reversed their decision and returned the money to the heirs. Rabbi Yohanan rebuked him, saying he had acted as though it were a matter of Torah law that must be corrected.

16.event: A woman whose husband could not father children demanded her marriage contract from Rabbi Ami.
16.turn: When he said she was not commanded to have children, she asked who would care for her in old age.
16.outcome: Rabbi Ami ruled that in such a case the husband is forced to divorce her and pay.
16.summary: A woman came before Rabbi Ami asking for a divorce and her marriage contract payment because her husband could not give her children. He told her to go away, since women are not commanded to have children. She answered by asking what would become of her in old age. Rabbi Ami then ruled that in such a case the husband is compelled to divorce her.

17.event: A son-in-law passed by the entrance of his father-in-law's house, and Rav Sheshet had him flogged.
17.turn: There were rumors about him and his mother-in-law.
17.summary: A man walked past the door of his father-in-law's house, and Rav Sheshet had him flogged. The reason was that rumors already linked him to his mother-in-law, and walking by fed them.
17.missing: It is a bare report cited in a legal discussion; the rumors explanation is the Gemara's.

18.event: Rabbi went to study Torah with Rabbi Elazar ben Shamua.
18.turn: The students ganged up on him like fighting roosters and did not let him learn.
18.outcome: He managed to learn only one teaching from the mishna.
18.summary: Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi recalled going to study with Rabbi Elazar ben Shamua. The other students banded together against him like aggressive roosters and would not let him learn. He came away with just one teaching: Rabbi Eliezer's ruling about a hermaphrodite.

19.actor: The daughter of Nakdimon ben Guryon
19.event: The Sages allotted Nakdimon ben Guryon's daughter four hundred gold coins for perfumes for a single day.
19.turn: Instead of complaining she blessed them, or perhaps mocked them, saying they should pledge the same for their own daughters.
19.summary: When the Sages set aside four hundred gold coins from her late husband's estate for the perfume expenses of Nakdimon ben Guryon's daughter for one day, she told them to allot the same for their own daughters. The Sages responded Amen.

20.actor: Rav Anan bar Tahalifa and Rav Ashi
20.event: Each stood before his teacher when a strong-smelling dish was brought, and the teacher shared it.
20.turn: Without being given some, each would have been endangered by craving.
20.outcome: They were given some and were not harmed.
20.summary: Rav Anan bar Tahalifa recalled standing before Mar Shmuel when a mushroom dish was brought; had Shmuel not given him some, his craving would have endangered him. Rav Ashi told the same about turnip slices in vinegar served to Rav Kahana.
20.missing: These are brief first-person anecdotes used as evidence; they have little narrative development.
